decidedBy: Essenthos, 2026-09-30, on the names a dataset lists a verse for where no word of ours named that record: each occurrence read against every record of the name by claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5-5, neither seeing the other's answer, and a third time by claude-opus-5-5 where the two differed. No person read them
policy: A word names the one its verse names. Where the verse, its passage or the list it stands in identifies the record, the word is that record's, and an answer a weaker pass had written there gives way. Where the two readings named different records, or the text leaves it open, the word is left as it was.
source: Essenthos, on the names a dataset lists a verse for, each occurrence read against its verse by claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-opus-5-5 independently, and a third time by claude-opus-5-5 where the two differed, 2026-09-30

rulings.why: 'the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan' (GEN 10:7) names the son of Raamah, as this record's line says; the Sheba of GEN 10:28 is a son of Joktan.
'Arioch king of Ellasar' names the city-kingdom Ellasar; no Asshur or Assyria is named here.
'Arioch king of Ellasar' names the city-kingdom Ellasar, as in GEN 14:1.
'Melchizedek king of Salem' names the place Salem; Genesis does not say Salem is Jerusalem (only PSA 76:2 'In Salem...in Zion' in another book, which is not evidence here).
'Ephron the son of Zohar' (GEN 23:8), the seller of the cave of Machpelah, is the person this record names; GEN 25:9 repeats 'the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite'.
'And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan' (GEN 25:3): Sheba is a son of Jokshan, which is this record's line.
Letushim is named among 'the sons of Dedan', the record's own line; the plural form is the list's.
Leummim is named among 'the sons of Dedan', the record's own line; the plural form is the list's.
'These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal...' names the man Seir, father of the Horite chiefs, not a mountain.
'these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom' gives Seir as the forefather, continuing 'the sons of Seir the Horite' (GEN 36:20).
'the sons of Gad; Ziphion, and Haggi, Shuni, and Ezbon, Eri, and Arodi, and Areli' lists Areli as a son of Gad, this record's line.
'Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah' (EXO 38:22) is the father of Bezalel, as EXO 35:30 says in the same words.
Hur the grandfather of Bezaleel, of the tribe of Judah: the words repeat EXO 31:2 and 35:30, which the record already holds.
'Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak' names Anak as the ancestor of those sons, which is this record's own verse.
'the children of Anak' names the ancestor Anak whose descendants the spies saw, as in NUM 13:22.
'the giants, the sons of Anak' names the ancestor Anak of the descendants seen in Hebron (NUM 13:22).
'Of Areli, the family of the Arelites' among 'the children of Gad': word 7 is the ancestor Areli (son of Gad, GEN 46:16), word 10 the clan 'the Arelites'.
'Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad' is the record's daughter of Zelophehad (NUM 27:1).
'Mahlah, Tirzah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad' (NUM 36:11); NUM 27:1 lists Milcah among his daughters.
Word 6 is the plural 'Anakims' ('the children of the Anakims'), the people; word 18 'the children of Anak' names the ancestor Anak.
'they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor' (DEU 23:4) is Balaam's father (NUM 22:5), not Bela's father of Edom.
'Japhia king of Lachish' is the king of the conquest named in JOS 10:3, as that record's line says; not David's son nor the border town.
'the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron' names Anak as Arba's son, matching JOS 21:11.
'the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak' names the ancestor Anak twice, as in NUM 13:22.
'the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak' names the ancestor Anak twice, as in NUM 13:22.
'he expelled thence the three sons of Anak' names the ancestor Anak, whose three sons are Ahiman, Sheshai, Talmai (NUM 13:22).
'the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed' (JDG 1:35): the house of Joseph is Joseph son of Jacob's line, as in JDG 1:22-23 'the house of Joseph'; no other Joseph candidate fits.
'the man Micah had an house of gods' is the man of mount Ephraim of JDG 17:1, whose money became the image 'in the house of Micah' (JDG 17:4).
'he came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah' is the same man as JDG 17:1 and 17:4, the owner of the image and the house of gods.
'And Micah said unto him, Whence comest thou?' is the householder of mount Ephraim (JDG 17:8, 17:1) who hires the Levite.
'Micah said unto him, Dwell with me, and be unto me a father and a priest' is the man of the house of JDG 17:1 and 17:8.
'Micah consecrated the Levite... in the house of Micah': both words name the man of mount Ephraim in whose house the Levite lived (JDG 17:1, 17:4).
'Micah consecrated the Levite... in the house of Micah': both words name the man of mount Ephraim in whose house the Levite lived (JDG 17:1, 17:4).
'Then said Micah, Now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest' is the man of JDG 17:1 and 17:12.
'mount Ephraim, to the house of Micah' with the Levite priest (JDG 18:3-4) is the man of JDG 17:1, 17:8 and 17:12.
'by the house of Micah... the young man the Levite' is the house on mount Ephraim of JDG 18:2 and 17:8, the man of JDG 17:1.
'Thus and thus dealeth Micah with me, and hath hired me, and I am his priest' is the man who hired the Levite (JDG 17:10), the man of JDG 17:1.
'mount Ephraim, and came unto the house of Micah', where the ephod and teraphim were (JDG 18:14), is the house of JDG 17:1, 17:5.
'the house of the young man the Levite, even unto the house of Micah' is the house on mount Ephraim of JDG 17:8 and 18:13, the man of JDG 17:1.
'these went into Micah's house, and fetched the carved image, the ephod, and the teraphim' is the house of the man of JDG 17:1, 17:5.
'a good way from the house of Micah, the men... near to Micah's house': both words name the man whose house held the image (JDG 18:18), the man of JDG 17:1.
'a good way from the house of Micah, the men... near to Micah's house': both words name the man whose house held the image (JDG 18:18), the man of JDG 17:1.
'said unto Micah, What aileth thee, that thou comest with such a company?' addresses the man whose gods and priest were taken (JDG 18:24), the man of JDG 17:1.
'when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back unto his house' is the man who lost his gods and priest (JDG 18:24), of JDG 17:1.
'they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest which he had' is the man of JDG 17:1 whose priest was the Levite (JDG 17:12).

'Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh ... priests to the tribe of Dan' (JDG 18:30) is the record's own verse; jehonathan-10 adds descent from Moses, which this verse does not say, so it looks like a duplicate.
'Micah's graven image, which he made' names the man Micah (idol of Micah) who made it (JDG 17:4-5); the image itself is the phrase, not this word.
'Ahiah, the son of Ahitub ... the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD's priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod' (1SA 14:3) is the priest, as ahijah-7's line says.

'Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli' (1SA 14:3) matches the record's line: son of Phinehas, grandson of Eli, father of Ahijah; the Ahitubs of Zadok's line are sons of Amariah.
'Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD's priest in Shiloh' names Eli's son Phinehas (1SA 1:3; 4:4).
Samuel 'sanctified Jesse and his sons' (1SA 16:5) and looked on Eliab, with Jesse calling Abinadab next (16:8); 1SA 17:13 names Eliab the firstborn son of Jesse.
'Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also' (2SA 1:4): Saul's son, the record with 65 verses naming Saul's son.
'Saul and Jonathan his son be dead' (2SA 1:5): Saul's son Jonathan.
'for Saul, and for Jonathan his son' (2SA 1:12): Saul's son Jonathan.
'over Saul and over Jonathan his son' (2SA 1:17): Saul's son Jonathan.
'the bow of Jonathan ... the sword of Saul' (2SA 1:22), in David's lament over Saul and Jonathan his son (2SA 1:17): Saul's son.
'Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant' (2SA 1:23), the lament of 2SA 1:17 over Saul and Jonathan his son: Saul's son.
'O Jonathan, thou wast slain in thine high places' (2SA 1:25), in the lament over Saul and Jonathan his son (2SA 1:17): Saul's son.
'my brother Jonathan' (2SA 1:26), David's lament over Saul and Jonathan his son (2SA 1:17): Saul's son.
'Joab returned from following Abner' with 'Abner and his men' (2SA 2:29) is Saul's army captain; Ram is not written here.

'Saul's son had two men that were captains of bands: the name of the one was Baanah ... the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite' (2SA 4:2) is Ish-bosheth's captain; Heleb's father is a Netophathite (2SA 23:29).
'Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son ... lame ... Mephibosheth'; the second, 'the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan', is the same Saul's son; both words name Saul's son.
'Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son ... lame ... Mephibosheth'; the second, 'the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan', is the same Saul's son; both words name Saul's son.
'the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah' came to Ishbosheth's house (2SA 4:5) are the captains of 2SA 4:2, not Heleb's father of 2SA 23:29.
'Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped' (2SA 4:6), the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite of 4:2 and 4:5, are Ish-bosheth's two captains.
'David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite' (2SA 4:9) is the captain of 2SA 4:2, not the Netophathite Heleb's father.
'the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon' lists David's sons; 1CH 3:5 repeats the list with Shimea.
'these be the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon' (2SA 5:14): a son of David, this record's line.
'born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammuah, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon' lists David's sons; 1CH 3:5 repeats it.
'the house of Saul ... for Jonathan's sake'; 2SA 9:3 'Jonathan hath yet a son' lame, and 9:6 'Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul': Saul's son.
'any of the house of Saul ... Jonathan hath yet a son, which is lame' (2SA 9:3); 9:6 calls Mephibosheth 'the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul': Saul's son.
'Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul' (2SA 9:6): Jonathan is named as Saul's son.
'for Jonathan thy father's sake ... all the land of Saul thy father' (2SA 9:7), said to Mephibosheth, 'the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul' (9:6): Saul's son.
'Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul', spared for the oath between David and Jonathan, is Jonathan's son (2SA 4:4), not Rizpah's son of verse 8.
'Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul' and 'between David and Jonathan the son of Saul' (2SA 21:7): both words name Saul's son.
'Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul' and 'between David and Jonathan the son of Saul' (2SA 21:7): both words name Saul's son.
'the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son' (2SA 21:12), slain with Saul in Gilboa: Saul's son.
'the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son' (2SA 21:13), as in 21:12 where Saul was slain in Gilboa: Saul's son.
'the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they ... in the sepulchre of Kish his father' (2SA 21:14): Saul's son.
'Jonathan the son of Shimeah the brother of David slew him' (2SA 21:21): David's nephew, matching this record's line, not Saul's son or any other Jonathan.
'Jonathan the son of Shimeah the brother of David'; 2SA 13:3 says 'Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother', so Shimeah is David's brother, Jesse's son, not Mikloth's son of 1CH 8:32.

'The Tachmonite ... chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite' matches this record's line (first of the thirty, Tahchemonite); Jashobeam is not named here, and the two Jashobeam records (Korahite, son of Zabdiel) do not fit.

'Jonathan the son of Abiathar the priest' (1KI 1:42) matches this record's line and 2SA 15:27; jehonathan-4 reads as a duplicate record of the same man, and its 'last of Eli's line' is not in the verse.
This Jonathan who 'answered and said to Adonijah' is the one just named 'the son of Abiathar the priest' (1KI 1:42); jehonathan-4 looks like a duplicate of the same man.
'Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar trees ... king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities' (1KI 9:11); both words name the king of Tyre, not the craftsman of 1KI 7:13.
'Hiram the king of Tyre had furnished Solomon with cedar trees ... king Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities' (1KI 9:11); both words name the king of Tyre, not the craftsman of 1KI 7:13.
'Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel' is jehoram-2; 'Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah' is jehoram, King of Judah, son of Jehoshaphat.
'Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah' and 'Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah' both name the king of Judah; no other candidate is a king of Judah.
'Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel' is jehoram-2; 'Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah began to reign' is jehoram, King of Judah and son of Jehoshaphat.
'Jehoshaphat being then king of Judah' and 'Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah' both name the king of Judah; no other candidate is a king of Judah.
'Ahaziah the king of Judah' who fled from Jehu (2KI 9:27), and 'Joram the son of Ahab' reigned when Ahaziah began over Judah (2KI 9:29); not the king of Israel, Azariah or Jehoahaz.
'smote him in Samaria... with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites' has Argob as a man with Pekah, not the region of Bashan.
'And the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan' (1CH 1:9) makes Sheba a son of Raamah, matching this record's line (GEN 10:7), not a place or the other Shebas.
'And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan' (1CH 1:32) makes Sheba a son of Jokshan, this record's line.
'Shobal the father of Kirjathjearim' among 'the sons of Caleb the son of Hur' (1CH 2:50, 2:52) is the son of Hur, this record's line, not the Edomite Shobal son of Seir.
'Shobal the father of Kirjathjearim had sons; Haroeh, and half of the Manahethites' (1CH 2:52) lists Haroeh as a son of Shobal, though the Hebrew word also reads 'the seer'.
'And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah' (1CH 4:6), Ashhur's wife (4:5): a son of Ashhur and Naarah, this record's line.
'And Naarah bare him Ahuzam, and Hepher, and Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah' (1CH 4:6) lists Haahashtari as a son of Ashur and Naarah (4:5), the only candidate.
'the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maachathite' among the sons of Hodiah's line: the gentilic 'the Maachathite' marks a man, as this record's line says.
'Ziza the son of Shiphi, the son of Allon, the son of Jedaiah' (1CH 4:37) is a man in the Simeonite princes' list, matching the allon record; the others are places or other men.
'the sons of Shemidah were, Ahian, and Shechem, and Likhi, and Aniam' (1CH 7:19): Shechem is a son of Shemida, which is this record's line.

'And Gedor, and Ahio, and Zacher' (1CH 8:31) follows the sons of the father of Gibeon and his wife Maachah (8:29-30), and the parallel list 1CH 9:37 gives 'Gedor, and Ahio, and Zechariah, and Mikloth'.
'Uthai the son of Ammihud, the son of Omri, the son of Imri, the son of Bani, of the children of Pharez the son of Judah' (1CH 9:4) names the Perez descendant, bani-3.
'of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David ... Ezer the first, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third' (1CH 12:8-9) is the Gadite warrior who went to David.
'Thine are we, David, and on thy side, thou son of Jesse' (1CH 12:18), next to 1CH 12:17, is the son of Jesse who was king; not the tent.
'And Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel': the word is 'adversary', written without the article, acting as a person; this record's own line is this verse.

'The fourth to Izri, he, his sons, and his brethren, were twelve' (1CH 25:11) stands in the lot list of the singers' families, and Zeri is a son of Jeduthun in 1CH 25:3; the only candidate and the same name.
'Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David' names a son of David; jerimoth-4 is this man, and jeremoth-13 describes the same man under another spelling.
'Iddo the seer concerning genealogies' (2CH 12:15) under Rehoboam and Jeroboam is the same book's 'visions of Iddo the seer against Jeroboam the son of Nebat' (2CH 9:29).
'Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam began Abijah to reign over Judah' (2CH 13:1) and he fights Jeroboam, so this is the king of Judah, son of Rehoboam (2CH 12:16).
'the story of the prophet Iddo' (2CH 13:22) for Abijah, son of Rehoboam, continues the same book's sources by Iddo the seer for Solomon and Rehoboam (2CH 9:29, 12:15).

'the same is Micaiah the son of Imla' (2CH 18:7), the prophet the king hates, is the man fetched here; micah-5 (son of Imlah) looks like a second record of the same man, but the verses are attached to micaiah.
'the messenger that went to call Micaiah' continues 2CH 18:8 'Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla', the prophet of 18:7, who answers in 18:13.
The king addresses 'Micaiah, shall we go to Ramothgilead' - the man fetched in 18:8, 'Micaiah the son of Imla' (18:7); the Hebrew spelling Micah here is a variant of the same name.
'Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests' to withstand 'Uzziah the king' (2CH 26:17-18) is the priest who opposed Uzziah, not Uzziah himself (azariah-3).
'Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, looked upon him, and, behold, he was leprous' (2CH 26:20) is the chief priest of the Uzziah scene (26:17-18), not the king, who is 'him'.
'Mahath the son of Amasai' among the Levites 'of the sons of the Kohathites' under Hezekiah is the Kohathite father of Mahath.
'of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi' in Hezekiah's Levites (2CH 29:12) is a Merarite father of Kish in his reign; abdi (1CH 6:44, son of Malluch, Ethan's line) is not tied to this verse.
'Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter toward the east' is the eastern gatekeeper; the record of Shallum's father (1CH 9:19) has no Imnah or eastern gate.
'Hilkiah and Zechariah and Jehiel, rulers of the house of God, gave unto the priests for the passover offerings' (2CH 35:8) under Josiah is this record's line.

'Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethaneel, his brethren... chief of the Levites, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings' (2CH 35:9) is the chief Levite giving offerings under Josiah, as this record says.
'Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethaneel, his brethren... chief of the Levites' gave oxen for Josiah's passover (2CH 35:7-9), matching this record's line of a chief of the Levites under Josiah.
'Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, chief of the Levites, gave unto the Levites for passover offerings' (2CH 35:9) in Josiah's passover is this Levite chief, as this record's line says.
Josiah's son made king (36:1) who reigned three months: the king's record. A second record, joahaz-2, describes the same king under this spelling.
Eliakim's brother whom Necho carried to Egypt is Josiah's son of 36:1: the king's record, as 36:2.

'Which came with Zerubbabel: Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah ... Rehum, Baanah' (EZR 2:2) is one of the men returning from captivity, matching baanah-3's line; the covenant sealer is a later list (NEH 10:27).
'the children of Nephusim' stands in the run of family names 'the children of Asnah, ... Mehunim' (2:48-52) of the temple servants, as this record's line says; it is the only candidate and fits.
'The children of Solomon's servants: ... the children of Sophereth' (EZR 2:55) names the ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants, as this record's line says.
'the sons of Henadad, with their sons and their brethren the Levites' (EZR 3:9) matches the Levite Henadad whose sons include Binnui (NEH 3:24, 10:9); Hodaviah is not written in this verse.
'Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak' who began to build is the Jeshua who returned with Zerubbabel (EZR 2:2, 3:8, 4:3, 10:18).
'repaired Ezer the son of Jeshua, the ruler of Mizpah, another piece over against the going up to the armoury' (NEH 3:19) is the wall-repairer of this record's line.
'Who came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah ... Nehum, Baanah' (NEH 7:7) retells the returning list of EZR 2:2, so this is the same returning leader, baanah-3.
'the children of Nephishesim' follows 'Besai, ... Meunim' in the same sequence as EZR 2:50 ('Nephusim'), so it is the same family; the only candidate and its line fits.
'The children of Solomon's servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth' (NEH 7:57) repeats the list of EZR 2:55, naming the same ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants.
'Malluch, Harim, Baanah' among 'the chief of the people' who sealed the covenant (NEH 10:14-27) is the sealing chief, as baanah-4 says; the text does not tie him to the returner of NEH 7:7.

'Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God' (NEH 13:7-8) is the Tobiah of NEH 13:4, allied with Eliashib, the opponent of NEH 2:10; tobijah-4 looks like a duplicate line.

'I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah' (NEH 13:13) is a Levite treasurer; no father is given to tie him to the other Pedaiahs.
'the son of Eliashib the high priest' in the days of Nehemiah and Sanballat (NEH 13:28); NEH 13:4,7 also name Eliashib the priest acting in Nehemiah's time, matching this record.
'smote all the firstborn in Egypt; ... the tabernacles of Ham' (PSA 78:51) sets Ham in parallel with Egypt, and PSA 105:23 'the land of Ham' speaks of the same country, so Ham names Egypt.
Kept: the verse as printed has Agur speak 'unto Ithiel and Ucal', and the record is that addressee; both readings note the word may be read otherwise.
'O Immanuel' is the name given in 7:14, which the record holds; the reading of the name as 'God with us' in 8:10 is the name's meaning, not another bearer.
'Then came Jeremiah from Tophet, whither the LORD had sent him to prophesy' (JER 19:14) is the prophet of the book, whom JER 20:1 has Pashur hear prophesying.
'Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the LORD' (JER 20:1) names the priest father of Pashur, as this record's line says.
'Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah' and the quoted 'Zion shall be plowed' is the prophet of Moresheth of MIC 1:1; micaiah-7 is the same man under another spelling.
'the prophet Jeremiah said unto the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests' in the temple is the prophet of the book of Jeremiah, the man of JER 28:5.
'Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name' is the father of the false prophet, not Zephaniah's father Maaseiah (JER 29:25).
'the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door' matches the record's line exactly.
'Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him' is the prophet; in JER 36:5 Jeremiah commands Baruch.
'Baruch in the book the words of Jeremiah' are the words Jeremiah the prophet commanded him to read (JER 36:8), so the prophet of the book.
'the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe' (JER 36:10), restated as 'Gemariah the son of Shaphan' in 36:12; not Gemariah son of Hilkiah (JER 29:3).
'Delaiah the son of Shemaiah' among the princes who heard Jeremiah's scroll (JER 36:12) is the father of Delaiah, exactly this record's line.
'Zedekiah the son of Hananiah' (JER 36:12) names the father of a prince sitting in the scribe's chamber in Jehoiakim's time, as this record's line says.
'Jaazaniah the son of Azur, and Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people' (EZK 11:1) is this son of Azzur, distinct from Jaazaniah son of Shaphan (EZK 8:11).
Azur the father of Jaazaniah, prince of the people: the record of that line. A second record, azzur-4, says the same of the same man.
'Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people' (EZK 11:1); EZK 11:13 says 'Pelatiah the son of Benaiah died'.
'Pelatiah the son of Benaiah, princes of the people' (EZK 11:1; again EZK 11:13) names the father of Pelatiah; David's Benaiah and the Levite and returnee Benaiahs are not his father.
'Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were thy merchants' among 'the men of Arvad', Tarshish, Dedan are lands or peoples trading with Tyre, like the place Javan with Tubal in ISA 66:19, not the man.
'Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they were thy merchants' (EZK 27:13) names a trading land or people beside Javan and Meshech, as 'Meshech and Tubal' in EZK 38:3, not the son of Japheth.
'the king made Daniel a great man ... ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and chief of the governors over all the wise men' (DAN 2:48) is the prophet of the book; Ezra's Daniel is a priest.
Word 19 writes Shadrach, the name given to Hananiah of Judah in DAN 1:6-7 ('unto Hananiah, of Shadrach'), one of the three cast into the furnace (DAN 3:20).
Meshach is the Babylonian name given to Mishael, one of Daniel's three companions (DAN 1:6-7), the same three as 'Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego' cast into the furnace here (DAN 3:20-23).
'Nebuchadnezzar the king was astonished' - the king who cast the three men into the furnace, not the golden image.
'Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God' (DAN 6:23) is the prophet of the book, in both places.
'Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God' (DAN 6:23) is the prophet of the book, in both places.
'he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son' (HOS 1:3) is Hosea's wife, not Japheth's son.
'Zephaniah the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah' (ZEP 1:1) names the prophet's father; Cushi father of Shelemiah (JER 36:14) is a different line.
'Then spake Haggai the LORD's messenger' (HAG 1:13), after 'the words of Haggai the prophet' (1:12), is the prophet of the book, not Haggi son of Gad.
The unclean spirit (MRK 5:8) answers 'My name is Legion: for we are many', which is the record's line.
Word 2 is 'Judas of James' (Judas the brother of James), one of the twelve in this list; word 5 is 'Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor', the betrayer record.
The unclean spirit in the man (LUK 8:29) answers 'Legion: because many devils were entered into him', the same Gerasene episode as the record's line.
'Judas saith unto him, not Iscariot': one of the Twelve at the supper and not the betrayer, the Judas the record holds (LUK 6:16, ACT 1:13).
The apostles' list: the James beside John is the son of Zebedee (ACT 12:2 'James the brother of John'); both readings agree on all three names of the verse.
'James the son of Alphaeus' of the apostles' list, as MAT 10:3; both readings agree on all three names of the verse.
'Simon the Zealot' (word 29) among the eleven apostles in ACT 1:13, with Peter separately named (word 13), is the zealot disciple of this record's line; Peter is written Petros, not Simon.
'Judas the brother of James', as LUK 6:16 lists Judas of James; both readings agree on all three names of the verse.
'Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing' who drew away people and perished (ACT 5:37) is the man who rose up in the days of the census, not any other Judas.
'with one Simon a tanner' (ACT 9:43): the tanner in Joppa, this record's line, as ACT 10:6 also says.

The men of Cornelius 'made enquiry for Simon's house' (ACT 10:17) and ask whether Simon surnamed Peter is lodged there (10:18); Peter lodges 'with one Simon a tanner' (9:43, 10:6), so the house is the tanner's.
'call hither Simon, whose surname is Peter' (word 7) is Peter; 'he is lodged in the house of one Simon a tanner by the sea side' (word 15) is the tanner (ACT 9:43, 10:6).
'Sopater Pyrrhou, a Berean': the Greek genitive Pyrrhou after Sopater's name gives his father, as this record's line says; the King James omits it.
'Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas' greets a Christian of Rome, the person Paul sends greetings to (ROM 16:14).
'unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer' - the addressee of the letter, Paul's fellow worker.
'the departing of the children of Israel' (sons of Israel) is the people's exodus, the nation descended from Jacob.
'the harlot Rahab... when she had received the spies with peace', after 'the walls of Jericho fell down' (HEB 11:30), is the harlot of Jericho of JOS 2:1.
'Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way' is the harlot who hid the spies (JOS 2:1).
'his name that sat on him was Death' (word 15) names the rider of the pale horse; 'with death' (word 39, plague) is the common noun, not the name.
